front: Passa lá em casa qualquer dia!
pronunciation: PAH-sah LAH eng KAH-zah kwahl-KEHR JEE-ah!
back: Drop by my place sometime!
context: Integration test #1: this is usually friendly politeness, not a real invitation. Wait for a date and an address before you show up.

front: Vamos marcar um café, sim! Te chamo.
pronunciation: VAH-mooz mahr-KAHR oong kah-FEH, SEENG! chee SHAH-moo.
back: Let's definitely get coffee! I'll message you.
context: 'Vamos marcar' is often a warm way to end a chat with no concrete plan. If no date is set, it may never happen, and that's normal.

front: Vou ver e te falo.
pronunciation: VOH VEHR ee chee FAH-loo.
back: I'll see and let you know.
context: Often a soft 'no'. Brazilians avoid saying a direct 'não' to invitations; reading this subtext is a real fluency skill.

front: A gente se fala!
pronunciation: ah ZHEHN-chee see FAH-lah!
back: Talk to you later!
context: A standard goodbye. Like 'see you around', it doesn't commit to anything specific.

front: Me vê um pingado e um pão na chapa, por favor.
pronunciation: mee VEH oong peen-GAH-doo ee oong POWNG nah SHAH-pah, pohr fah-VOHR.
back: I'll have a coffee with a splash of milk and a buttered toasted roll, please.
context: Classic São Paulo bakery order. 'Me vê' (literally 'see me') = I'll have. 'Pingado' = coffee with a 'drop' of milk.

front: Desce mais uma gelada aqui, chefe!
pronunciation: DEH-see MAHYZ OO-mah zheh-LAH-dah ah-KEE, SHEH-fee!
back: Bring us another cold one, boss!
context: Bar language: 'descer' (come down) = to bring/serve, 'gelada' = ice-cold beer. Waiters are often called 'chefe' or 'amigo'.

front: Essa é a saideira, juro!
pronunciation: EH-sah EH ah sahy-DAY-rah, ZHOO-roo!
back: This is the last one, I swear!
context: 'Saideira' = the last round before leaving. Ritually, it's almost never the last one.

front: Bora rachar a conta?
pronunciation: BOH-rah rrah-SHAHR ah KOHN-tah?
back: Shall we split the bill?
context: 'Rachar' (to crack, split) = to divide equally. Remember the 10% service charge is usually added to the bill.

front: Vamos fazer uma vaquinha para o presente da Ana.
pronunciation: VAH-mooz fah-ZEHR OO-mah vah-KEE-nyah PAH-rah oo preh-ZEHN-chee dah AH-nah.
back: Let's chip in for Ana's present.
context: 'Vaquinha' (little cow) = a group collection of money. Online fundraisers are also called 'vaquinhas'.

front: Ô, de casa! Tem alguém aí?
pronunciation: OH, jee KAH-zah! teng ahl-GENG ah-EE?
back: Hello, anybody home?
context: Traditional way to call at a house without a doorbell, especially in small towns.

front: Com licença, quem é o último da fila?
pronunciation: kohng lee-SEHN-sah, KENG EH oo OOL-chee-moo dah FEE-lah?
back: Excuse me, who's last in line?
context: Asking this is the polite way to join a disorganized queue at a clinic, bank or bakery.

front: Ele me deu um bolo: fiquei esperando uma hora e ele nem apareceu.
pronunciation: EH-lee mee DEH-oo oong BOH-loo: fee-KAY ehs-peh-RAHN-doo OO-mah OH-rah ee EH-lee NENG ah-pah-reh-SEH-oo.
back: He stood me up: I waited an hour and he didn't even show up.
context: 'Dar um bolo' (to give a cake) = to stand someone up.

front: Ela levou um fora do crush e ficou arrasada.
pronunciation: EH-lah leh-VOH oong FOH-rah doo KRAHSH ee fee-KOH ah-rrah-ZAH-dah.
back: She got turned down by her crush and was devastated.
context: 'Levar um fora' = to be rejected; 'dar um fora' = to reject someone. 'Crush' is fully adopted slang.

front: Ele simplesmente sumiu, me deu um perdido.
pronunciation: EH-lee seem-plehz-MEHN-chee soo-MEE-oo, mee DEH-oo oong pehr-JEE-doo.
back: He just disappeared on me; he ghosted me.
context: 'Dar um perdido' = to disappear on someone (also 'dar ghost'). 'Sumir' = to vanish.

front: Peguei ranço dele depois daquela discussão.
pronunciation: peh-GAY RRAHN-soo DEH-lee deh-POYZ dah-KEH-lah jees-koo-SOWNG.
back: I can't stand him anymore after that argument.
context: 'Pegar ranço' (to catch rancidness) = to develop an aversion to someone. Very current slang.

front: Tô passada com essa notícia!
pronunciation: TOH pah-SAH-dah kohng EH-sah noh-CHEE-syah!
back: I'm shocked by this news!
context: 'Estar passado/a' = to be stunned or shocked. Informal and expressive.

front: Ela lacrou na resposta e ninguém mais teve argumento.
pronunciation: EH-lah lah-KROH nah rrehs-POHS-tah ee neen-GENG MAHYS TEH-vee ahr-goo-MEHN-too.
back: She nailed that comeback and nobody had anything left to say.
context: 'Lacrar' (to seal) = to win a discussion with an unbeatable line. Internet slang.

front: Ele só posta foto na academia, é muito biscoiteiro.
pronunciation: EH-lee SOH POHS-tah FOH-too nah ah-kah-deh-MEE-ah, EH MOOY-too bees-koy-TAY-roo.
back: He only posts gym photos; he's such an attention-seeker.
context: 'Biscoiteiro' (cookie-seeker) = someone fishing for likes and praise, from 'dar biscoito' (to feed attention).

front: Quando cobrei o dinheiro, ela fez a egípcia.
pronunciation: KWAHN-doo koh-BRAY oo jee-NYAY-roo, EH-lah FEHZ ah eh-ZHEEP-syah.
back: When I asked for the money back, she pretended not to hear.
context: 'Fazer a egípcia' (to do the Egyptian) = to act like nothing happened, looking away like a profile in Egyptian art.

front: Rolou a maior treta no grupo da família.
pronunciation: rroh-LOH ah mah-YOHR TREH-tah noo GROO-poo dah fah-MEE-lyah.
back: A huge fight broke out in the family group chat.
context: 'Treta' = fight, drama. 'Rolar' = to happen. Family WhatsApp groups are famous battlegrounds.

front: Ela armou o maior barraco no meio da festa.
pronunciation: EH-lah ahr-MOH oo mah-YOHR bah-RRAH-koo noo MAY-oo dah FEHS-tah.
back: She made a huge scene in the middle of the party.
context: 'Armar um barraco' = to cause a loud public scene.

front: Deu ruim: o sistema caiu bem na hora da apresentação.
pronunciation: DEH-oo rroo-EENG: oo sees-TEH-mah kah-EE-oo BENG nah OH-rah dah ah-preh-zehn-tah-SOWNG.
back: Things went wrong: the system crashed right during the presentation.
context: 'Deu ruim' = it went badly; 'deu bom' = it worked out. Very common slang.

front: Sextou! Partiu praia?
pronunciation: sehs-TOH! pahr-CHEE-oo PRAHY-ah?
back: It's Friday! Beach, anyone?
context: 'Sextou' (it Fridayed) celebrates the start of the weekend. 'Partiu' + place = let's go to.

front: Fala sério, você acreditou nessa história?
pronunciation: FAH-lah SEH-ryoo, voh-SEH ah-kreh-jee-TOH NEH-sah ees-TOH-ryah?
back: Come on, you believed that story?
context: 'Fala sério' (speak seriously) = come on / you can't be serious.

front: Nem a pau que eu vou trabalhar no feriado!
pronunciation: NENG ah POW keh EH-oo VOH trah-bah-LYAHR noo feh-ree-AH-doo!
back: No way am I working on the holiday!
context: 'Nem a pau' = no way, not a chance. Informal.

front: Tô nem aí para o que os outros pensam.
pronunciation: TOH NENG ah-EE PAH-rah oo keh ooz OH-troos PEHN-sowng.
back: I couldn't care less what other people think.
context: 'Não estar nem aí' = to not care at all. Usually shortened to 'tô nem aí'.

front: Valeu pela força, tamo junto!
pronunciation: vah-LEH-oo PEH-lah FOHR-sah, TAH-moo ZHOON-too!
back: Thanks for the help, I've got your back!
context: 'Valeu' = thanks. 'Dar uma força' = to help. 'Tamo junto' = we're in this together.

front: Mó calor hoje, né?
pronunciation: MOH kah-LOHR OH-zhee, NEH?
back: It's so hot today, right?
context: 'Mó' = 'maior' (huge), used as an intensifier in youth slang, especially in Rio and São Paulo. Weather is the safest small-talk topic.

front: Para de me zoar, eu tô falando sério.
pronunciation: PAH-rah jee mee zoh-AHR, EH-oo TOH fah-LAHN-doo SEH-ryoo.
back: Stop teasing me, I'm serious.
context: 'Zoar' = to tease, mock, mess around. 'Zoeira' = joking around.

front: Ele vive pagando de rico, mas está na pindaíba.
pronunciation: EH-lee VEE-vee pah-GAHN-doo jee RREE-koo, mahs ehs-TAH nah peen-dah-EE-bah.
back: He's always showing off like he's rich, but he's broke.
context: 'Pagar de' = to pose as, show off as. 'Estar na pindaíba' = to be broke.

front: Pode pendurar na conta? Pago no fim do mês.
pronunciation: POH-jee pehn-doo-RAHR nah KOHN-tah? PAH-goo noo FEENG doo MEHS.
back: Can you put it on my tab? I'll pay at the end of the month.
context: 'Pendurar (na conta)' = to buy on credit at a local shop. 'Comprar fiado' means the same.

front: Esse vestido caiu como uma luva em você.
pronunciation: EH-see vehs-CHEE-doo kah-EE-oo KOH-moo OO-mah LOO-vah eng voh-SEH.
back: That dress fits you like a glove.
context: 'Cair como uma luva' = to fit perfectly, also used for situations: 'a ajuda caiu como uma luva'.

front: Tô de molho em casa por causa da gripe.
pronunciation: TOH jee MOH-lyoo eng KAH-zah pohr KOW-zah dah GREE-pee.
back: I'm laid up at home because of the flu.
context: 'Ficar/estar de molho' (soaking) = to stay in to rest and recover.

front: Ela tem jogo de cintura para lidar com clientes difíceis.
pronunciation: EH-lah teng ZHOH-goo jee seen-TOO-rah PAH-rah lee-DAHR kohng klee-EHN-cheez jee-FEE-says.
back: She knows how to handle difficult clients smoothly.
context: 'Jogo de cintura' (hip movement, as in samba) = flexibility, the ability to handle tricky situations gracefully.

front: Calma, a gente dá um jeito.
pronunciation: KAHL-mah, ah ZHEHN-chee DAH oong ZHAY-too.
back: Relax, we'll find a way.
context: 'Dar um jeito' = to find a solution or workaround. Related to the famous, sometimes criticized, 'jeitinho brasileiro'.

front: O tal do jeitinho brasileiro pode ser criatividade ou pura malandragem.
pronunciation: oo TAHL doo zhay-CHEE-nyoo brah-zee-LAY-roo POH-jee SEHR kree-ah-chee-vee-DAH-jee oh POO-rah mah-lahn-DRAH-zheng.
back: The so-called Brazilian 'jeitinho' can be creativity or pure trickery.
context: Integration test: understanding both sides of the 'jeitinho' (resourcefulness vs bending rules). 'O tal do' = the so-called.

front: Ponho a mão no fogo por ela: é a pessoa mais honesta que conheço.
pronunciation: POH-nyoo ah MOWNG noo FOH-goo pohr EH-lah: EH ah peh-SOH-ah MAHYZ oh-NEHS-tah keh koh-NYEH-soo.
back: I'd vouch for her with my life: she's the most honest person I know.
context: 'Pôr a mão no fogo por alguém' (put your hand in the fire) = to vouch completely for someone.

front: Ele fez corpo mole e deixou todo o trabalho para nós.
pronunciation: EH-lee FEHS KOHR-poo MOH-lee ee day-SHOH TOH-doo oo trah-BAH-lyoo PAH-rah NOHS.
back: He slacked off and left all the work to us.
context: 'Fazer corpo mole' (to make your body soft) = to avoid effort, slack off.

front: Fizeram a obra a toque de caixa por causa da eleição.
pronunciation: fee-ZEH-rowng ah OH-brah ah TOH-kee jee KAHY-shah pohr KOW-zah dah eh-lay-SOWNG.
back: They rushed the construction work because of the election.
context: 'A toque de caixa' (to the drumbeat) = in a great hurry, often carelessly.

front: Isso é conversa fiada, ninguém vai cumprir essa promessa.
pronunciation: EE-soo EH kohn-VEHR-sah fee-AH-dah, neen-GENG VAHY koom-PREER EH-sah proh-MEH-sah.
back: That's just empty talk; nobody's going to keep that promise.
context: 'Conversa fiada' = idle talk, hot air. 'Cumprir uma promessa' = to keep a promise.

front: Depois da promoção, ele está com a bola toda.
pronunciation: deh-POYZ dah proh-moh-SOWNG, EH-lee ehs-TAH kohng ah BOH-lah TOH-dah.
back: After the promotion, he's on top of the world.
context: 'Estar com a bola toda' (to have the whole ball) = to be at your peak, very confident or popular.

front: Ah, vá! Não acredito que você passou no concurso!
pronunciation: AH, VAH! NOWNG ah-kreh-JEE-too keh voh-SEH pah-SOH noo kohn-KOOR-soo!
back: No way! I can't believe you passed the civil service exam!
context: 'Ah, vá!' (oh, go!) = no way!, expressing pleasant or skeptical surprise.

front: Deus me livre ter que acordar às cinco todo dia!
pronunciation: DEH-oos mee LEE-vree TEHR keh ah-kohr-DAHR AHS SEEN-koo TOH-doo JEE-ah!
back: God forbid I have to wake up at five every day!
context: 'Deus me livre' = God forbid / no way. A very common exclamation.

front: Manda um áudio que eu escuto quando sair da reunião.
pronunciation: MAHN-dah oong OW-jee-oo keh EH-oo ehs-KOO-too KWAHN-doo sah-EER dah rreh-oo-nee-OWNG.
back: Send me a voice message and I'll listen when I'm out of the meeting.
context: Brazilians love WhatsApp voice messages ('áudios'), sometimes several minutes long. 'Quando sair' = future subjunctive.

front: Tô chegando, cinco minutinhos!
pronunciation: TOH sheh-GAHN-doo, SEEN-koo mee-noo-CHEE-nyoos!
back: I'm almost there, five minutes!
context: Integration test: 'tô chegando' and 'cinco minutinhos' are elastic. They can mean twenty minutes or more.

front: Que horas a festa começa de verdade?
pronunciation: keh OH-rahz ah FEHS-tah koh-MEH-sah jee vehr-DAH-jee?
back: What time does the party actually start?
context: At Brazilian parties, the time on the invitation and the real start time are often different. Ask a local!

front: Opa, tudo joia? Quanto tempo!
pronunciation: OH-pah, TOO-doo ZHOY-ah? KWAHN-too TEHM-poo!
back: Hey, everything good? Long time no see!
context: 'Opa' = hey (also 'oops'). 'Tudo joia?' = all good? 'Quanto tempo!' = long time no see!

front: Não precisa trazer nada, só a sua presença!
pronunciation: NOWNG preh-SEE-zah trah-ZEHR NAH-dah, SOH ah SOO-ah preh-ZEHN-sah!
back: No need to bring anything, just yourself!
context: Polite formula; arriving with a drink or dessert is still a nice gesture at a Brazilian get-together.

front: Pô, que vacilo! Esqueci o seu aniversário.
pronunciation: POH, keh vah-SEE-loo! ehs-keh-SEE oo SEH-oo ah-nee-vehr-SAH-ryoo.
back: Man, my bad! I forgot your birthday.
context: 'Vacilo' = a slip-up, a careless mistake; 'vacilar' = to mess up. 'Pô' is a mild, very common interjection of frustration.

front: Já é de casa, pode abrir a geladeira à vontade.
pronunciation: ZHAH EH jee KAH-zah, POH-jee ah-BREER ah zheh-lah-DAY-rah AH vohn-TAH-jee.
back: You're family now; feel free to open the fridge.
context: 'Ser de casa' = to be like family. 'À vontade' = freely, make yourself comfortable. The final integration test passed!
